verdicts.reason: A keeps the large rust quote mark, a ~35px side margin and a three-line quote that reads cleanly. Its flaws are a wide dead gap between the mark and the text, empty space at the bottom, and attribution text that is tiny at this size. B shrinks the quote mark to a token size and runs the quote in long lines that nearly touch the left edge (about 12px margin). It also crams the attribution right under the quote and leaves the top half of the canvas empty, so it looks like a shrunk copy.

A has the same problems as before: a tiny quote mark, a cramped left margin of about 12px, long quote lines and the attribution jammed under the text, with the whole group sunk below an empty top half. B uses larger type, a bold quote mark and proper side margins. But B's group is weighted low, leaving the top ~40% empty, and its attribution is very small.

A has strong hierarchy: a big quote mark, then a large three-line quote, then the attribution, all with even margins. Its weakness is balance: everything sits in the top half and the bottom ~40% is dead space, and the attribution is tiny. B has a tiny quote mark, text crammed almost to the edges, the attribution tight to the quote, and an empty upper half.
